newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends lower, supply contradicts swaps.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends lower, supply contradicts swaps.

text.p: NWE naphtha ended slightly lower on Tuesday, tracking a modest selloff in crude, as some traders braced for a possible squeeze in physical prices starting Wednesday.
But several end-users said petrochemical demand was lacklustre and local supplies were growing, which should counter the recent gains in Feb swaps prices.
"I think it's overdone and artificially supported. It is not backed up by the physical market," one trader said. "Everything is pointing to a $2 (a barrel) crack and not $3. It is ridiculously high."
Feb swaps ended about $1 lower at $228/$229 a tonne, but held its wide $8 backwardation to March, which ended at $220/$221. April finished at $214/$215.
Cargoes were notionally unchanged at $226/$230 cif, but no deals were heard at these levels.

"If you look at the spread to gasoline, it's negative. If you look at the arb to the States, it's not open," the trader said, who added that Brazil was not keeping up with its normal, heavier purchases.
"Local supplies are also adding up," he said.

He said the following were available in NWE -- four, 5,000-10,000 parcels of Russian material of at least 65 paraffins, by February 15; fob material for the rest of the month totalling 20-30,000 tonnes; 10,000-20,000 tonnes of Dow spec material; and 20,000 tonnes, possibly 40,000, of paraffinic material on offer by another seller.
"Still there is length in the market," a broker said, who, nonetheless, said the paraffinic material now available was not out of the ordinary and not bearish.
Russian material is also normally offered into NWE.
But sources said there was speculation that one trader may try to boost the physical market on Wednesday when a 60,000 tonne Skikda cargo it owns is loaded. The cargo was believed sold to Petrobras.
Anticipation of that buying has already boosted swaps prices and kept cargoes about $63 or 23 percent above its year-ago levels.
The trader said another 50,000 tonne Skikda cargo was expected to be loaded Feb 24-26, though this was not confirmed, on top of two other large cargoes of 50,000-60,000 tonnes from Skikda this month.
